issue_context.title: client-go/workqueue needs priority queue
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

There is such a scenario, we have many clusters, up to 100,000, and the cluster has regular health checks, and the number of work coroutines is limited. When the work coroutine is doing cluster health check processing, there are new cluster starts to be created, we need to prioritize the newly created cluster, so we need a priority queue.



### What did you expect to happen?

We need to get high priority items from the queue for processing

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

None

### Anything else we need to know?

None

### Kubernetes version

None

### Cloud provider

None

comments:
/sig api-machinery
Would it not be possible to implement it as part of your project? The workqueue package provides interfaces to implement. Not sure if there is a need for it in Kubernetes.

For those writing controllers directly against client-go, yes, the workqueue is entirely a choice of the controller author.

Even so, I think it is fair to ask if it would be valuable to make client-go offer a variant of workqueue that has some sort of prioritization.

I think if it is also fair to ask if a simpler solution would solve the OP's problem.  What about just submitting the health check entries to the work queue at a limited rate --- or, if that is already the case, at a lower rate?  I think it is arguable that the other work should not starve the health checks.

/kind feature
/priority awaiting-more-evidence

/assign @277631272 
since you have a PR already: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109349

> 
@[MadhavJivrajani](https://github.com/MadhavJivrajani)
The priority queue was originally a part of the project. Later, it was found that many scenarios were involved. At the same time, it was found that many crds also needed to be processed according to the priority. Therefore, I felt that if it was integrated into client-go, different people could be used for this scenario. to use

@[MikeSpreitzer](https://github.com/MikeSpreitzer)
I feel that prioritizing some important tasks, because these tasks need to be processed in real time, and the number of these important tasks is usually relatively small. And for a large number of tasks, it is usually the second most important, even if these tasks wait for a while, it should be fine

review_comments:
the priority queue should be based on a heap 

https://pkg.go.dev/container/heap#example-package-PriorityQueue

so it can scale well

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priority_queue
Thanks a lot, very good suggestion, I will refactor priority_queue.go based on heap.

(1) There needs to be a comment defining the behavior of this type of queue.

(2) As far as I can tell from looking at the implementation here, the behavior is that items are ordered by priority *ONLY* --- the ordering of the Add calls is not relevant.  Remember that a heap does not preserve ordering between items that compare equal.  I find the irrelevance of ordering of Add among equal-priority items to be surprising.

(3) I see nothing in the package comment about priority queues.

(4) The package comment is outdated: it speaks of a single type of queue, but this package already implements multiple types of queue.
This field is not used for anything in this package.  And being private, clients can not access it either.  I suggest removing it.
